items.description: Patrick Flynn's birthplace: Ireland (1850 and 1860 censuses) vs. Pennsylvania (1908 death certificate)
items.independence_analysis: The two census records (1850, 1860) are independent original sources with different enumerators. The death certificate is a third independent original source. However, the census informants are likely the same household member (Thomas Flynn or wife), so the two census assertions may share a single informant — potentially not fully independent for this fact.
items.weighing_analysis: The census records are contemporary recordings made near the time of Patrick's birth, while the death certificate was created 63 years later. The census informant was likely a household member with firsthand knowledge (primary or indeterminate), while the death certificate informant (son-in-law) is clearly secondary for birth facts. Two contemporary sources outweigh one later recollection by a secondary informant.
items.resolution_rationale: Ireland is accepted as the birthplace. The 1908 death certificate birthplace of 'Pennsylvania' is rejected as a likely error by the son-in-law informant, who may have confused Patrick's place of residence with his place of birth, or may not have known Patrick was born in Ireland before immigrating as a young child.

Here is what the search-external-sites agent found and recommends:

---

**Matricula Online — Browse for Wilhelm Kuhlmann's 1836 Marriage in Ochtrup**

Matricula is a free archive of scanned Catholic parish registers, but it is a **browse site, not a name-search site**. Here's how to find the record:

1. **Open the site:** [https://data.matricula-online.eu/de/](https://data.matricula-online.eu/de/)
2. Click **Suchen → Ortssuche** and type **Ochtrup** as the place.
3. Confirm you are in the **Catholic parish, Diocese of Münster**.
4. Select the **marriage register (Trauungen)** and the volume covering **1836**.
5. Page through the entries for that year, looking for **Wilhelm Kuhlmann** as groom.
6. Once you find the right page, save it as a PDF (Cmd+P / Ctrl+P → Save as PDF) and upload it here so the record can be logged and extracted.

**Note:** Matricula doesn't confirm in advance whether Ochtrup is in its holdings, so a missing parish on the site doesn't mean the record doesn't exist.

---

**Fallback if Matricula doesn't have it:**

FamilySearch has filmed the Ochtrup Catholic church book — **"Kirchenbuch, 1667–1875," film 876540**, which covers baptisms, marriages, and deaths **1804–1865** (including 1836). This film is **not online**; it can only be viewed at a **FamilySearch Center or affiliate library**.

FamilySearch's indexed collection **"Germany, Marriages, 1558–1929"** could also be searched directly. (Ochtrup civil registers on FamilySearch begin in 1874, so those won't help for 1836.)

---

**Next step:** Open the Matricula link, navigate to the Ochtrup marriage register for 1836, and upload a capture. The agent can then log it and pull out the details.

output.text_response:
Here's what the search-external-sites agent found and set up for you:

**Search logged as log_006.**

Open this Ancestry search link:

👉 **[Pennsylvania Wills & Probate Records for Thomas Flynn in Schuylkill County](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/8800/?name=Thomas_Flynn&deathplace=Schuylkill%2C+Pennsylvania%2C+United+States)**

This searches Ancestry's **"Pennsylvania, U.S., Wills and Probate Records, 1683–1993"** collection. (No year filter is available on that collection page, so scan the results yourself for dates in the 1870–1890 range.)

**What to look for:**
- A Thomas Flynn with a will or estate file dated roughly 1870–1890 in Schuylkill County
- Listed heirs, executors, or children — especially Patrick, Mary, and James

**Next steps:**
1. Log in to Ancestry if prompted
2. Scroll through the results page (top to bottom and back)
3. Save the page as a PDF (Cmd+P on Mac / Ctrl+P on Windows → Save as PDF)
4. Upload the PDF here

Once you upload the capture, the agent will triage the results and identify which record(s) to examine more closely.

**Also noted:** FamilySearch holds "Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683–1994," but it is browse-only (no name index). That could be searched page-by-page via search-images if Ancestry turns up nothing.

items.description: Patrick Flynn's birthplace: Ireland (1850 and 1860 censuses) vs. Pennsylvania (1908 death certificate)
items.independence_analysis: The two census records (1850, 1860) are independent original sources with different enumerators. The death certificate is a third independent original source. However, the census informants are likely the same household member (Thomas Flynn or wife), so the two census assertions may share a single informant — potentially not fully independent for this fact.
items.weighing_analysis: The census records are contemporary recordings made near the time of Patrick's birth, while the death certificate was created 63 years later. The census informant was likely a household member with firsthand knowledge (primary or indeterminate), while the death certificate informant (son-in-law) is clearly secondary for birth facts. Two contemporary sources outweigh one later recollection by a secondary informant.
items.resolution_rationale: Ireland is accepted as the birthplace. The 1908 death certificate birthplace of 'Pennsylvania' is rejected as a likely error by the son-in-law informant, who may have confused Patrick's place of residence with his place of birth, or may not have known Patrick was born in Ireland before immigrating as a young child.
